CausalChain: EMT → Loss of miR-200 → Upregulation of ZEB1 → Acquisition of mesenchymal, stem-like properties and chemoresistance → Exosome-mediated miRNA transfer → Engineered exosomes delivering miR-200 mimics → Suppression of ZEB1 → Reversion of EMT to MET → Decreased stemness and increased chemosensitivity
Hypothesis: Engineered exosomes loaded with miR-200 family mimics can reverse EMT-induced drug resistance in cancer by suppressing ZEB1 expression, thereby reducing cancer stemness and restoring chemosensitivity.
Abstract: In many cancers, the epithelial‐to‐mesenchymal transition (EMT) not only contributes to metastasis but also endows tumor cells with stem cell‐like properties and chemoresistance. Several miRNAs, such as members of the miR‐200 family, are pivotal regulators of this process by targeting EMT transcription factors like ZEB1. Moreover, exosomes have emerged as natural carriers of miRNAs that modulate intercellular communication. Here, we propose a novel therapeutic strategy that exploits engineered exosomes loaded with miR‐200 mimics to reprogram mesenchymal, drug‐resistant cancer cells. By restoring miR‐200 levels, the hypothesis is that these exosomes can suppress ZEB1 expression, reverse EMT, diminish cancer stemness, and ultimately restore sensitivity to chemotherapy.
